How the plan fits together

Salary estimates take-home income. Budget turns expenses into a monthly plan. Invest moves available cash into registered accounts. Year combines these into bank and investment balances. Goals compare targets with the projection.

What the numbers assume

Amounts are CAD, rounded for display. Starting balances are January 1 balances. Recurring expenses are monthly averages. Returns compound monthly; future tax thresholds generally follow your inflation assumption. Salaries stop together at the younger person’s retirement age unless you keep an explicit work override.

Ontario includes basic and age credits, the health premium, and surtax. Other provinces use simplified estimates: additional senior, family and low-income credits are not included. Quebec includes QPP, EI, QPIP and the federal abatement, with CPP-based retirement-benefit estimates.

CPP/QPP depends on contribution history. OAS assumes full residency. Employer pensions, GIS, child benefits, self-employment payroll, investment fees, and unregistered accounts are not modelled automatically. Add known after-tax amounts in Year.

How the plan fits together

Salary estimates take-home income. Budget turns expenses into a monthly plan. Invest moves available cash into registered accounts. Year combines these into bank and investment balances. Goals compare targets with the projection.

What the numbers assume

Amounts are CAD, rounded for display. Starting balances are January 1 balances. Recurring expenses are monthly averages. Returns compound monthly; future tax thresholds generally follow your inflation assumption. Salaries stop together at the younger person’s retirement age unless you keep an explicit work override.

Ontario includes basic and age credits, the health premium, and surtax. Other provinces use simplified estimates: additional senior, family and low-income credits are not included. Quebec includes QPP, EI, QPIP and the federal abatement, with CPP-based retirement-benefit estimates.

CPP/QPP depends on contribution history. OAS assumes full residency. Employer pensions, GIS, child benefits, self-employment payroll, investment fees, and unregistered accounts are not modelled automatically. Add known after-tax amounts in Year.

How the plan fits together

Salary estimates take-home income. Budget turns expenses into a monthly plan. Invest moves available cash into registered accounts. Year combines these into bank and investment balances. Goals compare targets with the projection.

What the numbers assume

Amounts are CAD, rounded for display. Starting balances are January 1 balances. Recurring expenses are monthly averages. Returns compound monthly; future tax thresholds generally follow your inflation assumption. Salaries stop together at the younger person’s retirement age unless you keep an explicit work override.

Ontario includes basic and age credits, the health premium, and surtax. Other provinces use simplified estimates: additional senior, family and low-income credits are not included. Quebec includes QPP, EI, QPIP and the federal abatement, with CPP-based retirement-benefit estimates.

CPP/QPP depends on contribution history. OAS assumes full residency. Employer pensions, GIS, child benefits, self-employment payroll, investment fees, and unregistered accounts are not modelled automatically. Add known after-tax amounts in Year.
